native_result.report:
The quadratic Theorems A and B and Corollary C are established in their stated scope. The complete embedded n100 argument also withstands independent reconstruction; its earlier verdict and hash were not used as assumptions. This does not establish P06.2 recognition, unrestricted finite-Galois ascent, higher-dimensional separable ascent, or ascent through an infinite separable completion.

The finite tensor-product argument is valid without reducedness or a spectral norm: bounded coordinate functionals identify the tensor topology with a finite complete direct sum. The invariant-algebra calculation remains valid in characteristic two. The unit criterion uses actual maximal ideals. Separability gives the stated field-factor decomposition of each quadratic fibre; finite-dimensional norm equivalence and the powers argument establish uniqueness of its extending absolute values. The invariant-idempotent argument establishes transitivity. Hausdorffness, compact inverse images, and the compact-complement shrinking construction follow as written, without a covering-space assumption.

The comparison of ordinary forms on the E-carrier and its restricted K-structure is justified by common unit charts and compact-image nullity. It concerns this same carrier and does not assume descent through π. Curve purity is established separately: a zero-dimensional minimal component downstairs would be isolated, contradicting purity; the reduced tensor embeds into a product of fields; minimal primes upstairs contract to minimal primes downstairs; integral dimension preservation then gives one-dimensional components upstairs. Goodness, strictness, separatedness, boundarylessness, and their ordinary-open restrictions satisfy the hypotheses of canonical integration at every tower stage.

Under (H), all three coefficient pairs have unit entries and every pair has determinant of absolute value one. Thus two traces cannot both have magnitude below the maximum. The trace identity (4) holds in both required cases: unequal magnitudes give no cancellation, while equal magnitudes force at least one selected trace to attain the maximum. Shrinking makes both selected traces units. Applying the identity to each f_i and f_if_j yields every δ_iδ_j, with the real factor 1/2 in (5). Simultaneous interchange is precisely δ↦−δ; pairing the factors of every even-total-degree monomial proves polynomial descent. No division by two in the valued field occurs.

The singleton-fibre construction correctly symmetrizes a Euclidean smooth coefficient on a fixed upstairs chart. Gaussian convolution and finite exponential Taylor sums give uniform control of derivatives through order two; averaging preserves that control on the invariant box. For two-point fibres, disjoint conjugate opens and structural-sheaf gluing give invariant analytic units and exact local scalar descent. The argument establishes the required antecedents for both fibre cases.

Compact approximation uses a finite ordinary-open partition near the compact image of the test support. The products extend smoothly by zero because their cutoff supports are closed compact subsets of their defining opens. Equation (9) holds both near and outside the support. The fixed unit lists, coefficient domains and cutoffs give the differentiated error bound by the product rule. If a chart for the entire sum is desired, intersect the finitely many relevant chart neighbourhoods and combine their unit lists; compactness gives a finite fixed refinement. This is a harmless clarification of the phrase ‘same fixed chart’, not an additional approximation theorem.

On each calibrated curve cell, contraction gives H(v,v). The displayed Cauchy–Schwarz bound dominates its absolute value by rMε_j times the positive form ξ. Its mass is finite on each fixed compact chart. The calibration retains the actual finite degrees and all tangent-coordinate normalization factors; the inequality does not replace them with point counts. Zero-dimensional faces carry no smooth top-form mass, and the dimension-one factorial is 1. Summing the finite bounds proves total-variation convergence with fixed compact support. Boundedness of the continuous multiplier on that support proves convergence of the differentiated pairings.

The averaging and transport steps use the correct distinct normalizations. Ground-field restriction multiplies the calibration by 2; the degree-one K-analytic automorphism preserves that restricted calibration. Dividing the resulting real measure identity by 2 establishes invariance of the E-pairing. Scalar extension itself has no factor 2: CLD 15.3.1 applies to the differentiated compact smooth test and gives (13). Averaging, approximation and this identity establish ascent against every upstairs scalar test. Compact pullback and the same identity establish descent. Finite quadratic towers therefore iterate without requiring their composite to be Galois. The finite-separable descent remark is also justified by the finite étale purity argument.

For n100, the compositum construction supplies an extending seminorm bounded by the full tensor seminorm. The image of A⊗K L0 is dense, and finite Frobenius powers determine values there, proving uniqueness and the homeomorphism even when the completion is not algebraic. Approximation below each unit’s positive minimum norm preserves its absolute value exactly. A common finite purely inseparable coefficient extension then gives τ_f=q⁻¹τ_g∘π. Pulling back by this linear scaling contributes q⁻(a+b) in bidegree (a,b), including every differential. Compact-image nullity proves injectivity; ordinary sheaf gluing proves surjectivity and exact supports. Corresponding cofinal affinoid neighbourhoods establish purity. The differentiated top-measure identity proves the Hessian and both first-current equivalences in all stated dimensions. The Artinian thickening example, perfectness argument, and completed-perfection residue-field example are correct.

The relevant primary statements and proof bodies were opened in the specified editions. In particular, the degree proof uses actual finite fibre algebras, the generic-length proof tensors an actual length filtration, and the calibration proofs retain degree and determinant factors. The supplemental boundary-equality assertion uses GR 2.12; its proof has the valid indirect geometric dependency on Conrad–Temkin 11.5 listed below. That dependency supplies no ordinary-form descent.

The declared comparison notes were also checked: GJR 14.2 concerns weakly smooth forms, GJR 15.11 starts with Thuillier subharmonicity and produces weakly smooth approximants, CLD 16.3.3(d) concludes G-tropical regularity, and GR normalization results do not transport a continuous Hessian current. One harmless wording correction is required: GR 3.4.1 includes the alternative ‘identically −∞’; its finite real-valued specialization used here has no exception. [GR v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2#page=11), [GJR v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.05741v3#page=75), [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2#page=447).

No substantial mathematical repair is required. Artifact hashes, finite diagnostics and compilation claims contribute no proof verification to this verdict.

Affinoid neighbourhoods form a basis in a good analytic space; ordinary opens are analytic domains; analytically separated spaces are Hausdorff. CLD v2, §§11.1.1, 11.1.5, 11.1.7, 11.2.2.

Affinoid fibre products are computed by completed tensor products. For a complete analytic extension L/k, M(A)L=M(A⊗̂kL), scalar projection is surjective, and inverse images of analytic domains have their base-change structures. A finite extension of k is analytically separable exactly when it is separable. CLD v2, §11.1.9.
A finite Banach algebra over a k-affinoid algebra, endowed with its finite-module topology, is k-affinoid. Finite analytic morphisms are boundaryless. CLD v2, §11.4.4.

Strict affinoid analytic dimension equals Krull dimension; complete scalar extension preserves analytic dimension. For affinoid X with irreducible components Xi, dimx X=max{x∈Xi} dim Xi. Local analytic dimension is the minimum of dimensions of affinoid domains containing the point, and analytic domains preserve local dimension. Purity of dimension n means local dimension n at every point. CLD v2, §11.2.3.
For a morphism X→Y of k-analytic spaces and any analytic field extension L/k, ∂(XL/YL)⊆π⁻¹(∂(X/Y)); in particular ∂XL⊆π⁻¹(∂X). GR v2, §2.11(5′).

Ordinary CLD smooth forms are locally, on ordinary open neighbourhoods, smooth coefficient forms pulled back through affine tropical charts. They form ordinary-topology sheaves stable under wedge product, J, d′ and d″. Tropical pullback is functorial, respects the bigraded algebra structure, and commutes with these operators; affine analytic pullback preserves ordinary smoothness. CLD v2, §§3.3.12, 6.2.1–2.

On a topologically separated k-analytic space, every ordinary CLD smooth (p,q)-form has an ordinary open cover on which it is the pullback of a smooth real form on a paralinéaire subset through an analytic moment. In split torus coordinates, a moment is a finite list of analytic units. In bidegree (0,0), this gives local smooth functions of their logarithmic absolute values. CLD v2, Definition 12.2.1, Proposition 15.1.1(b), Corollary 15.1.2.

For a paralinéaire subset P of a finite-dimensional real affine space V and an ambient open U, restriction of coefficient forms modulo forms null on P injects into forms on U∩P, and is surjective if U∩P is closed in U. In particular this applies to smooth coefficients and compact moment images. CLD v2, Lemma 1.9.4.

For a tropical representation f*γ on a compact G-tropical space, coefficient nullity on f(X) is equivalent to zero pullback in the tropical-form presheaf. That presheaf is separated on compact G-covers. For an arbitrary G-tropical chart, zero image in the G-form sheaf is equivalent to coefficient nullity on every compact-domain image. CLD v2, Proposition 3.4.1, Corollary 3.4.2, Proposition 3.4.4.

A good Hausdorff analytic space is locally holomorphically separated. On such a space, for a closed subset F countable at infinity, including a compact F, and an ordinary open cover (Ui) of F, there exists a locally finite family of nonnegative ordinary smooth functions θi with compact support contained in Ui and sum one near F. CLD v2, §15.2.2 and Corollary 15.2.9.

A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space has the canonical calibrated tropical structure of level n and its associated integration and current theory. Canonical skeletal calibrations are standard, compatible with analytic-domain restriction, and on convenient top cells use the positive actual finite degrees of suitable moment projections. CLD v2, §§14.3.2–5 and Theorem 15.7.1.

On a tropical space of level n, locally integrable multipliers define integration currents by pairing with compact ordinary smooth complementary-degree forms; continuous real multipliers are locally integrable. Differentiation by duality gives zero-Hessian tests in degree (n−1,n−1), zero-d′ tests in degree (n−1,n), and zero-d″ tests in degree (n,n−1), up to the fixed duality signs. CLD v2, §§7.1 and 7.3.5.

For a zero-dimensional local analytic fibre, the local degree of a morphism is the dimension of its actual finite fibre algebra over the completed residue field. For complete scalar extension, if y maps to x and xL lies over x, degy(f)=Σz∈fL⁻¹(xL)∩q⁻¹(y) degz(fL); summing yields degx(f)=degxL(fL). CLD v2, §§13.3.1–2 and Lemma 13.3.3.

Under complete scalar extension of an analytic space, at an upstairs generic component lying over a downstairs component, the actual generic length ℓL of the structure sheaf is μℓ, where ℓ is the downstairs generic length and μ is the generic multiplicity of the base change of the downstairs reduction. No reduction of the upstairs structure sheaf is taken. CLD v2, Lemma 13.2.8 specialized to OX.

For an analytic space X of level n, a skeletal subset Σ with canonical calibration μ, and a complete extension L/k, the scalar-extended skeletal subset ΣL constructed in CLD 12.9.11 has canonical calibration μL satisfying π*μL=μ, where π* denotes pushforward. CLD v2, Proposition 14.3.6.

For an analytic space X of level n, a complete extension L/k, and an (n,n)-form ω on XG with tropically Borel coefficients, scalar projection satisfies π*(ωL,Bor)=ωBor. If ω is locally integrable, π*(ωL,Rad)=ωRad. Here π* denotes pushforward and ωL is scalar-extension pullback. CLD v2, Proposition 15.3.1.

If F/k is finite and Z is an F-analytic space of level n, its same carrier Z0 with restricted k-analytic structure has the same analytic dimension and skeletal subsets, and canonical calibration μZ0=[F:k]μZ. Common smooth top forms consequently have Radon measures related by the same factor. CLD v2, Remark 14.4.3.

Let f:Y→X be a morphism between k-analytic spaces of level n, finite away from a Zariski closed subset of X of dimension less than n. For p∈{n−1,n} and a locally integrable (p,n)-G-form ω, f*ω is locally integrable and f*((f*ω)Rad)=dcf·ωRad, with pushforward on the outer f* and pullback on the inner f*. CLD v2, §15.4.1 and Proposition 15.4.3.

Every G-tropical chart on a compact G-tropical space of level n is pleasant and its tropical polyhedron is the n-dimensional part of its compact image. For a moment on a compact analytic space of level n, the relevant skeletal cell decomposition can be chosen finite and refined into convenient cells adapted to the image. CLD v2, §5.4.4 and §§14.1.8, 14.1.11–12.

For a pleasant chart f on a calibrated G-tropical space of level n and a coefficient (n,n)-form α, integration and the associated top Radon measure are obtained by contracting α with the induced calibration on its tropical polyhedron. When locally integrable, ftrop,*((f*α)Rad)=⟨α,μΠf⟩Rad; when integrable, ∫X f*α=∫Πf⟨α,μΠf⟩. CLD v2, Proposition 5.10.1.
For any k-analytic space X and any analytic field extension L/k, scalar projection satisfies π(∂XL)=∂X. GR v2, Lemma 2.12.

For any analytic field extension L/k and morphism g:X→Y of k-analytic spaces, g is boundaryless if and only if its scalar extension gL:XL→YL is boundaryless. Conrad–Temkin v2, Theorem 11.5, property (vii).
